You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687872/attempts/0874d736f6374307823ec7507ddf4822/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687872/attempts/0874d736f6374307823ec7507ddf4822/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's file. If it exists, run its transform on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. If there is no file, or its answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have received until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve recurring Continual-ARC grid instances with a task-id Python program library, demonstrations, and strict one-action replies.
---

# Continual-ARC instances

Use for each Continual-ARC puzzle instance, especially when task IDs may recur and their saved program can be reused.

1. Read the task ID, test grid, and attempt/demo counts. Check `programs/<task id>.py` first. If present, run its `transform(grid)` on the supplied test grid and submit exactly that result as the first task action; do not request demos or alter the saved file first.
2. If no program exists, or its submitted output is marked incorrect, request demonstrations as needed. Infer a rule from all observed pairs rather than guessing from one object. Transcribe grids without altering cells or row widths; assert that each parsed grid has the displayed dimensions before running the transform. Write or repair the task's Python file and execute it on every available demonstration, checking exact output equality. Then run it on the exact test grid and submit only that computed result. Emit puzzle actions directly as the required final-line JSON reply; shell commands or other tool calls do not request demos or submit an answer.
3. Track the verdict. After an incorrect submission, do not resubmit the same guess: revisit the rule and the input transcription, check dimensions/rows against the displayed grid, and use remaining demonstrations to disambiguate. Do not replace a known-good program with an unverified guess; require exact reproduction of every available pair before submitting a new output. A correct verdict ends the instance; save the program that reproduces all pairs at the task-ID path, replacing any older version if needed, then finish.
4. On every interaction, including demo requests and post-verdict turns, end with exactly one required JSON action. Use `finish` only after the instance is over; never add explanatory text if the evaluator requires exactly the action object.

Completion check: the submitted grid came from the task program; after success, the saved `transform` reproduces every received demonstration pair.
